rep.name: Richard Claessen
rep.location: Bulgaria; in the Netherlands for a week at the time of the call

setter.evidence: No setter code in the title, but the rep clearly worked from a written application — 'I read, if I'm correct, that you're 35, right?' and 'I also read that you sort of put down that if you don't change, like now, it's going to be harder and harder.' Whether a setter took that application or it was submitted directly is not established.

prospect.name: Anthony Acosta
prospect.location: Resident in Belgium; American; taking the call from Dubai while combining work and holiday
prospect.training_background: Active his whole life and a dancer from a young age. Currently does something four times a week but does not enjoy or do structured strength training, which he has never sustained — 'I always drop off after like a few weeks and then you start from ground zero again.' Has done a little kettlebell work with a personal trainer in the past and enjoyed it, but has not tried any of Trevor's published movements. Describes his deep core and muscle definition as strong and says his body composition changes quickly. Has followed Trevor's account for a while and booked after seeing consecutive posts about taking new clients.
prospect.medical: Functional scoliosis, self-disclosed, with a stated goal of learning to balance the two sides. Hypermobile rather than stiff — 'I'm too flexible' — with strong external rotation from dance but weak adductors and weak midline stabilisers, and difficulty with posterior pelvic tilt. No pain, injury or clinician was mentioned, and the rep did not ask about any of it.

signals: Already fit and operating professionally in the movement field; explicitly content with his current state — 'I'm pretty content with my body performance in my field' and 'I don't feel bad in my body'

Wants a specific capability added to an already strong base rather than a rescue: 'I want to be able to lift heavy things, move heavy things, and have the balance of flexibility, mobility, and strength'
Price was never a barrier and never commented on — he asked the cost as a neutral data point and refused on product capability alone
Measures success by skill and load progression rather than appearance: 'I would much rather know that I'm getting better at the skill of kettlebell... Composition, I care less about'

Departs from the archetype in one respect: he is a domain expert buying a narrow technical service, not a generalist buying transformation, which is why almost none of the programme's value proposition applied to him

goals.text: Learn kettlebell technique properly and be told when his form is wrong, especially before progressing in weight
Build consistency in strength training, which he has never sustained
Get progressive overload over time, which he has never achieved
See kettlebell weight progression week over week and month over month as the measure of success
Build stability and midline strength to offset being hypermobile — weak adductors and difficulty with posterior pelvic tilt
Gain awareness of how to balance the two sides of his body given functional scoliosis
Be able to lift and move heavy things, with flexibility, mobility and strength in balance
Train at home with minimal equipment
Enjoy the training, which he names as the precondition for sticking to it
Eat in a way that leaves him feeling full as a vegetarian, using volume and fibre

pains.text: Has never enjoyed strength training and therefore has never been consistent with it — 'from day one, I was not interested'
Drops off strength training after a few weeks and restarts from zero, never reaching progression
Hypermobility without matching stability; weak adductors and midline stabilisers
Functional scoliosis and side imbalance he wants to learn to manage
Struggles to feel full as a vegetarian and is working around it with volume, fibre and grains
Personal trainers in his area do not offer kettlebell-specific coaching
Being a practitioner himself, finds it hard to be the client — 'I need to be a client at a certain point as well'

objections.raw_quote: I mean, to be quite honest, I don't see the value in the individualized one for myself. Like, if I can send videos on a community, and if the one-on-one doesn't have that live, like, correction, then I don't really see the value, to be honest.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without challenge — 'Ah, check. No, that's understandable, right?' — and immediately redirected to the community tier, then gave both prices.

objections.raw_quote: To be honest, I'm not interested in either. I was looking for something a lot more just with live feedback. And not like all the time, but like I did expect some type of live feedback because I think that's important.
objections.rep_response: Disqualified gracefully and did not attempt to rebut — 'No, of course, if that's what you're looking for, then there's no use case in me trying to get you to do something, right?' He offered to check with the team whether any coach delivers one-to-one Zoom sessions and to follow up.

evidence: Explicit refusal of both tiers immediately after hearing prices: 'To be honest, I'm not interested in either.'
Reason given was product capability, not price: 'I was looking for something a lot more just with live feedback.'
Confirmed the missing feature was decisive — he asked 'for the community, is there an option to book a one-on-one live training with a coach in general?' and was told 'No, not really.'
Had already rejected the premium tier on value grounds before price was given: 'I don't see the value in the individualized one for myself.'
The rep did not contest the decision and disqualified cleanly.

Counter-evidence for a follow_up reading: he asked the rep to check whether any coach offers one-to-one Zoom and to email him, and the rep agreed to raise it at the team meeting. That is a genuine open thread, but it depends on a service the business does not currently offer, so the deal as presented is lost.
outcome.next_step: Rep to ask the team whether any coach offers live one-to-one Zoom sessions and to email or call the prospect with the answer.

notable.note: A product-fit loss that the rep himself recognised only afterwards. The prospect stated in his first answer that he did not want daily accountability, then asked for pricing and package options six separate times across fifteen minutes while the rep completed the scripted three-pillar presentation and gated the price behind a commitment check. What he actually wanted — periodic live video form correction — does not exist in either tier. There is a strong indication this is the prospect the same rep described to his manager three hours later, in the 06/30 coaching one-to-one, as 'a little bit zesty', confirmed in that call to mean gay: the timing fits, and the description given there — 'he was also looking for someone to jump onto one-to-ones, like, face-to-face like this, and review his whole workout while he's doing it' — matches this call precisely. In that same session the rep conceded 'I pitched for the sake of pitching' and the manager said the correct move was to disqualify at the point the need was stated.

quality.notes: Noticeably cleaner than the rest of this batch, with clear turn-taking through most of the call. Inversions do occur — most obviously around 00:13:19, where the rep's line 'I don't even see myself really needing to follow videos' is plainly the prospect's, and at 00:31:11 to 00:31:23, where an exchange about nationality and Dutch is swapped so that the rep appears to say 'I'm American'. Roles resolved from content. Height 177 cm and weight 82 kg were given in metric and converted to 70 in and 181 lb.
